questions.description: Knowing the injury type helps tailor the return-to-running plan appropriately (e.g., knee, ankle, stress fracture, shin splints).
questions.title: What type of injury are you recovering from?

questions.description: Understanding your current medical status helps determine whether professional sign-off is still needed before starting.
questions.title: Have you been cleared by a doctor or physio to run?

questions.description: The length of time off affects how gradually you need to rebuild fitness and load.
questions.title: How long have you been unable to run?

questions.description: For example, casual jogger, 5K runner, half-marathon or marathon trainer — this sets the baseline to work back towards.
questions.title: What was your running level before the injury?

questions.description: Such as completing a race, running a certain distance, or simply getting back to regular exercise.
questions.title: Do you have a specific goal you are working towards?

questions.description: For example, within 4 weeks, 3 months, or by a specific event date — this shapes the pace of the plan.
questions.title: What is your target timeframe for returning to full running?

questions.description: Knowing what cross-training or physiotherapy exercises are already in place helps build a complementary plan.
questions.title: Are you currently doing any other exercise or rehab?
